headline: The firm helping Reykjavík City says the attack probably used an AI tool and was stopped while still mapping systems; no suspect is named.
summary: Added Vísir's Nov 27 interview with Syndis's chief executive (s010, Tier 2, opened and read in full): c015 (Reported): artificial-intelligence tools were probably used, and the tool was likely still in an inspection and analysis mode when stopped, before it touched data; he also says nobody in particular is suspected and the attack was routed through other people's hacked computers, so s010 is added to c009. Same interviewee as RÚV (s009), so this is the firm's account, not independent corroboration. q004 stays open with c015. Site-wide banner (s004) re-read in a browser at about 6:09 AM ET: services still disrupted, financial-assistance applications unavailable; service stays down (c003, last_checked moved). No city notice newer than Nov 27 (s003); CERT-IS assessment (s008) unchanged, next due early Monday. mbl.is pieces of Nov 27 not checked: access blocked. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on the attack; Reddit not read (search refused).

headline: The firm helping Reykjavík City says attackers were stopped before stealing or encrypting data; the city has not said if any was taken.
summary: Added RÚV's Nov 27 interview with Syndis's chief executive (s009, Tier 2, opened and read in full): c013 (Reported): attackers stopped in the first steps, before stealing or encrypting data, few signs much data is involved; c014 (Reported): they broke into the city's cloud system, linked to other systems in Iceland they also entered, entry points still under investigation. q003 and q004 stay open with the new claims; q006's answer now mentions the linked systems. Site-wide banner (s004) re-read in a browser at about 4:11 AM ET: services still disrupted, financial-assistance applications unavailable; service stays down (c003, last_checked moved). No city notice newer than Nov 27 (s003). CERT-IS assessment unchanged, next due Monday. Vísir and a second RÚV piece of Nov 27 repeat the city notice. headline: Reykjavík City says attackers breached some of its systems on Nov 25; many online services are still disrupted while it restores them.
summary: New incident page. Reykjavík City's own notices of Nov 25, 26 and 27 (s001-s003, Tier 1, read in English and Icelandic): a serious cyberattack on several of its computer systems on Nov 25; digital service systems taken offline to protect systems and data; working with Syndis and CERT-IS; resetting all passwords and access keys; working out how the attackers got in and what data they may have accessed; most systems to return Nov 27 and over the weekend, the rest possibly early next week. The site-wide notice read Nov 28 at 3:25 AM ET (s004) still says online services are disrupted and online financial-assistance applications are unavailable, so service is down (c003). Vísir (s005, s006) interviewed CERT-IS and civil protection and carried the city's written answer that it did not know whether data was taken (c006, Reported). RÚV (s007) reports on unnamed sources that hackers got passwords and into a database; the city would not confirm (c007, Reported). No attacker named, no group claim, ransomware not mentioned (c009). Blue Lagoon attacked the same day; CERT-IS cannot say they are related; no source links 1984 Hosting (c010). CERT-IS keeps the national alert at uncertainty through the weekend (c011). Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated, on the city's own notices. incident_type attack; size Local. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on the Reykjavík attack; Reddit refused.
